notes: WHAT THIS FILE IS. The largest manufacturing plants in the 50 states and DC, ranked by people on one source: the 'annual average number of employees' each establishment reported to OSHA on Form 300A for 2025 (2024 where an establishment has no 2025 row), read from OSHA's published establishment files on disk (https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data). The figure is that employer's people at that address, offices on the site included, contractors not included. It replaces the earlier 99-plant file, which rested largely on Wikipedia. Web search was not available, so no figure in this pass was checked against a company page. THE TOP 100. 175 plants are ranked. Rank 100 has 3,350 people. Of the first 100, 87 rest on the OSHA figure, 12 on a figure the earlier file read on the company's own page or a government page dated 2024 or later (kept by rule, with the OSHA figure in the note), 0 on Wikipedia and 1 on a news report (Gulfstream Savannah, 13,000, which does not appear in OSHA's manufacturing rows). Across all 175: 153 OSHA, 18 company or government, 3 Wikipedia only (Pfizer Rocky Mount, Denso Manufacturing Michigan, Collins Aerospace Rockford), 1 news. TWO LIMITS ON 'THE 100 LARGEST'. (1) 11 large plants are real but could not be given coordinates and so are in `unplaced`, not in the ranking: Lyon Station Complex (6,114); NASSCO San Diego (4,110); Burns Harbor (4,003); Tyson Fresh Meats Dakota City (3,771); Mountaire Lumber Bridge (3,500); SK Battery America Commerce (3,127); Boeing Ridley Park (3,071); Mercury Marine Fond du Lac (2,941); Seaboard Foods Guymon (2,855); Howard Industries Laurel (2,733); McKee Foods Collegedale (2,674). Five of them (East Penn's Lyon Station complex, NASSCO, Burns Harbor, Tyson Dakota City and Mountaire Lumber Bridge) are larger than rank 100 and would push the cut-off up to about 3,430 if placed by hand. (2) OSHA shows only sites that filed: plants that did not file, or filed under a non-manufacturing code, are missing unless the earlier file had them. HOW IT WAS BUILT. Every NAICS 31-33 row in the two files was ranked by people and judged from the top down to 2,600 people, which gave 154 real plants; below 2,600 the only plants are those carried over from the earlier file, so the ranking is complete on this source only down to 2,600. Rows at one address for one company count as one plant; where a company files parts of one address separately the largest row was taken unless the parts are plainly one plant (noted on the plant). Merge with the earlier file: its company fields, plant names, coordinates and opening years are kept; its headcount is kept only where it came from the company's own page or a government page dated 2024 or later (Newport News Shipbuilding 26,000, Fort Worth Air Force Plant 4 19,000, BMW Plant Spartanburg 11,000, Ingalls Shipbuilding 11,000, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky 10,000, Gigafactory Nevada 8,060, Pratt & Whitney East Hartford 7,425, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana 7,380, Subaru of Indiana Automotive 6,500, Sikorsky Stratford 5,734, Hyundai Motor Manufacturing Alabama 4,200, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Texas 4,000, Samsung Austin Semiconductor 3,342, Austal USA Mobile 3,000, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Alabama 2,400, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Mississippi 2,400, Toyota Motor Manufacturing West Virginia 2,077, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Missouri 1,000); otherwise the OSHA figure is used and the earlier figure, with its source, is moved into the note (a figure that was 'read on Wikipedia only' is still marked so there). Economic-development lists and news reports were not treated as company or government pages, which is why Boeing Everett, Boeing Wichita, Raytheon Tucson, Textron Aviation, Rivian, Micron, Kia, Caterpillar Decatur, ADM and others now carry the OSHA figure.
